detail:
The Spondylitis Association of America describes itself as a funder of spondyloarthritis research aimed at reducing the long delay many people experience before diagnosis, improving treatments, and ultimately prevention. Projects it lists include work on the association between inflammatory bowel disease and spondyloarthritis across gastroenterology and rheumatology sites, and education programs helping radiologists and rheumatologists work together on MRI interpretation to hasten diagnosis.

Other funded directions include genetic and environmental studies, including a multi-investigator study of genetic susceptibility beyond the well-known HLA-B27 association, research into whether fungus or yeast plays a role in triggering spondyloarthritis, microbiome studies, and a national patient registry. The Association also convenes periodic Unmet Research Needs conferences at the National Institutes of Health to set priorities where knowledge gaps remain largest.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about spondyloarthritis research.

takeaways: shortening the diagnostic delay is a stated research priority
genetics research extends beyond the hla-b27 association
gut, microbiome, and ibd links are active study areas
research participation is optional; talk to your doctor about studies
title: Where ankylosing spondylitis research is heading
